followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain three distinct phases: the road-vehicle rule and two versions of pedestrian night hours. They do not describe a continuously closed crossing for every cohort. P1 excludes road vehicles in both directions while the initial notice excepts pedestrians and rail. P2/P3 restrict nighttime pedestrian passage; people already on the bridge could be processed after 23:00 under the earlier schedule. P1 retains 1 February 2024 onset and 23 February 2026 confirmation, a 753-day policy lower bound. P2’s 15 June 2026 endpoint is an exclusive schedule-version boundary; P3 is confirmed 13 August. Intermittent durations and overlapping totals remain withheld. Reconstruction is attributed to P1; traffic/staff allocation to P2/P3; explicit security purposes to P3. General war or migration context does not become a rationale for every phase. The vehicle notice and shared February customs page were freshly inspected; five other exact passages were reused. Government announcements and ERR accounts are traced to their named official origins, not treated as seven independent confirmations. All three phases remain unlocated and retain cohort-specific dated-evidence display rules. Neither Narva 2 nor railway geography is inherited.
